name: Slovenia
summary: Slovenia's electric car market grew quickly in 2025–2026: battery-electric cars were about 11% of new passenger cars in 2025 and almost 20% in January–August 2026, while Borzen offered purchase subsidies of up to €7,800 that were oversubscribed by August 2026. Home wallboxes are sold by energy companies, car importers, electrical installers and online shops; several sellers quote prices with basic installation at the reduced 9.5% VAT rate, and a separate Borzen grant covers 55% of the cost up to €1,000 per charging point, with requests already above the 2026 budget. Public charging is led by Petrol and Elektro Ljubljana's Gremo na elektriko network, alongside IONITY, Tesla and MOONcharge; published prices run from €0.22–0.35/kWh for AC and €0.45/kWh for DC at Gremo na elektriko to €0.43–0.73/kWh at IONITY.

subsidies.programme: Borzen JP SUB-EV26 – grants for electric vehicles (Climate Fund)
subsidies.who: Sklop A: any adult with permanent residence in Slovenia (not self-employed or registered for business). Sklop B: businesses, sole traders and public-law bodies (not direct state budget users).
subsidies.deadline: Applications from 18.6.2026 10:00 until funds are used or closure is announced; for vehicles over 45.000 € (sklop A) only applications filed by 31.8.2026.
subsidies.note: Budget 25.604.648,00 € (sklop A) and 8.000.000,00 € (sklop B). Vehicles bought from 1.1.2026 and first registered in Slovenia. Borzen's notice: requested amounts already exceed the available funds for both individuals and legal entities, so late applications may be rejected. Media report the ministry had no more Climate Fund money to top up the call (Siol, 08.08.2026) and that the subsidy period ended in August 2026 'at least for now' (Siol, 07.09.2026). No formal closure notice was found.
subsidies.source_title: Subvencije za e-vozila fizičnih in pravnih oseb 2026

subsidies.programme: Borzen JP SZPI 2026 – grants for private charging points (home chargers)
subsidies.amount: Individuals (sklop A): 55% of eligible purchase and installation costs, up to 1.000 € per charging point, max. 2 points (2.000 €). Businesses (sklop B): 55%, up to 1.300 € per charging point.
subsidies.who: Sklop A: adults with permanent residence in Slovenia and a tax number (not self-employed). Sklop B: self-employed persons, sole traders and legal entities.

buildings.topic: Own charger when the cable passes through common parts
buildings.text: When works in an owner's own unit also interfere with common parts of the building, the owner may not start them without the consent of co-owners holding more than half of the co-ownership shares in those common parts; the works must follow building rules and be professionally supervised.
buildings.law: Stanovanjski zakon (SZ-1), Article 15 (consolidated text valid from 13.08.2025)
buildings.source_title: 15. člen SZ-1 • Stanovanjski zakon - SZ-1 • Zakonodaja • Računovodstvo.net

buildings.text: Answering a 2017 citizen proposal on charging in apartment blocks, the Ministry of the Environment and Spatial Planning applied Article 15 of SZ-1: if the works also touch common parts, consent of co-owners holding more than half of the co-ownership shares is needed. It found no legal basis for requiring unanimous consent for a private charger.
Co-owners holding more than three quarters of the co-ownership shares decide on building works on common parts of a multi-apartment building that require a building permit.
buildings.law: Stanovanjski zakon (SZ-1), Article 29, as amended by SZ-1E (Uradni list RS, No. 90/2021, 4.6.2021)
buildings.source_title: Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Stanovanjskega zakona (SZ-1E)

buildings.topic: Changing the use of common parts
buildings.text: Consent of all co-owners is required for changes between common and individual parts, for special restrictions on the use of individual or common parts, and for changing the use of common parts.
buildings.law: Stanovanjski zakon (SZ-1), Article 29 (consolidated text valid from 13.08.2025)
buildings.source_title: 29. člen SZ-1 • Stanovanjski zakon - SZ-1 • Zakonodaja • Računovodstvo.net

buildings.text: A legal Q&A from the newspaper Dnevnik (republished on the Na novinah portal) says that, according to case law, changing the use of a parking area needs the consent of all co-owners; a shared charging project is a matter beyond ordinary management, and co-owners holding more than half of the shares in the common parts can ask a court to decide in non-contentious proceedings.
buildings.law: Stanovanjski zakon (SZ-1) and case law, as explained in the article
buildings.source_title: Polnjenje električnega avtomobila pred blokom | DNEVNIK - NA NOVINAH

buildings.topic: Metering: charging through the resident's own meter
buildings.text: In the same Q&A the resident's plan is to feed the garage charger from their own apartment, through their own electricity meter; the expert assesses such individual works under Article 15 of SZ-1.
buildings.source_title: Polnjenje električnega avtomobila pred blokom | DNEVNIK - NA NOVINAH

buildings.text: Avto magazin notes that the cost of shared electricity can be allocated by installing additional sub-meters (odštevalni števci), but that this is not always feasible; it names owners' consent as the biggest obstacle.
buildings.source_title: Električne polnilnice v večstanovanjskih stavbah - Kdaj lahko pričakujemo spremembe? - Aktualno - Avto Magazin

buildings.topic: Shared charging station named in housing law
buildings.text: The 2025 housing law amendment lists a 'skupna polnilna postaja' (shared charging station) among the common parts of residential and multi-apartment buildings, in the article on serious damage caused by tenants. It applies from 1.12.2025.
buildings.law: SZ-1G (Uradni list RS, No. 57/2025, 29.7.2025), amending Article 103 of SZ-1
buildings.source_title: Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Stanovanjskega zakona (SZ-1G)

buildings.text: Borzen's 2026 home-charger call has no specific provisions for multi-apartment buildings, co-owner consent or the building manager; the charger must be at the applicant's permanent residence or on property the applicant owns, and the applicant must remain its owner for at least five years.
buildings.law: Javni poziv JP SZPI 2026 (clean copy with 1st amendment)

buildings.text: A reader's account describes the steps taken in one building: consent of more than 50% of co-owners by co-ownership shares, design documentation (PZI), certified electrical measurements and a fire-safety assessment. The charger was connected to the existing apartment meter, and the building manager (upravnik) received the documentation afterwards. The rules were described as loose and fire-safety requirements as unclear.
buildings.source_title: Težava, ki jo bo treba rešiti, če bo električnih avtomobilov vse več - Žurnal24

buildings.text: The e-mobility association DeMS says charging in multi-apartment buildings is often handled through administrative limits or general bans instead of an individual technical assessment, and calls for a move 'from bans to technical conditions' based on European and IEC standards and fire-safety requirements.
buildings.source_title: Energetski zakon: Vsaka »nova rešitev« lahko dodatno oteži dostop do polnilnic v večstanovanjskih stavbah - DEMS

buildings.text: According to Avto magazin, the Efficient Use of Energy Act (ZURE) requires new buildings and major renovations with larger car parks to fit chargers or cable ducting on part of the parking spaces; for multi-apartment buildings the article cites ducting at every tenth parking space.
buildings.law: Zakon o učinkoviti rabi energije (ZURE); article not cited in the source
buildings.source_title: Električni avto in življenje v bloku - kakšne so možnosti in (predvsem) ovire? - Avto-magazin.si

buildings.text: No Slovenian company advertising a dedicated service for multi-apartment buildings (shared installation with per-resident billing) was found on the pages checked. Some sellers address blocks indirectly: Enertec recommends RFID/PIN-protected chargers for shared garages, EVJ notes RFID identification is useful in apartment blocks, and Plan-net Solar's enquiry form includes a multi-apartment building option.

policy.text: Slovenia's Act on Alternative Fuels Infrastructure and Promoting the Transition to Alternative Fuels in Transport (ZIAG) was published in Uradni list RS, No. 62/2023, on 6 June 2023.

Under the EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), each registered battery-electric car must be matched by at least 1.3 kW, and each plug-in hybrid by at least 0.8 kW, of publicly accessible charging power; the EU's Alternative Fuels Observatory tracks Slovenia against this fleet-based target.
policy.source_date: reference data: fleet Q1 2026, infrastructure July 2026

policy.text: According to Forbes Slovenia, the National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN) foresees about 93,000 new electric vehicles in 2026–2030, roughly three times as many as in the previous five years.

A 15 million € public call (JRPM IZVEN-TEN-T-2026, published 6 March 2026) funds publicly accessible charging outside the TEN-T road network with up to 100% co-financing (up to 10,000 € per AC point, 25,000 € per 50–150 kW DC point and 40,000 € per DC point above 150 kW), at least 10 charging points per project, 16 hours of daily public access, applications by 31 July 2026 and completion by 31 October 2027.

The Statistical Office site (stat.si) did not load; SURS figures are taken from media that quote SURS.
pisrs.si needs JavaScript and could not be read; law texts were checked in the Official Gazette (uradni-list.si) and in a legal database (racunovodstvo.net).
EAFO country pages show data only in interactive charts; EAFO charging-point numbers are quoted from Forbes Slovenia.
No exact count of battery-electric cars on the road was found; only a rounded figure (about 24,000, source not named) and a 2% fleet share.

2025 sales conflict: Forbes Slovenia (18.07.2026) says 2,700 new electric vehicles were sold in 2025, while AMZS, SURS-based and Eurostat-based reports give about 6,400 battery-electric cars; the Forbes figure was not used.
Public charging counts differ by dataset: EAFO (about 2,545 in December 2025, over 3,000 by mid-2026) versus the official register as mapped by DeMS (over 4,600 points in August 2026).
Petrol's public-charging price list did not render; Petrol per-kWh prices come from an undated comparison site and are unverified.
The Gremo na elektriko PDF price list is blocked by robots.txt; prices were taken from the operator's 'Vozniki' page (valid from 1.7.2023).

Energija plus (energijaplus.si and polnilnepostaje.energijaplus.si) returned server errors; its home-charger offer and public-charging prices were not verified (a copy on a third-party domain was not used).
The MOL Plugee Slovenia site (molplugee.si) timed out; MOL's network size and prices in Slovenia are unverified.
Eleport is named as an operator by Forbes Slovenia, but eleport.com shows no Slovenia-specific data.
Tesla Supercharger and MOONcharge per-kWh prices are not shown on the reachable pages; IONITY, Tesla and MOONcharge station counts in Slovenia were not found.
Motorway (DARS / TEN-T) charging coverage and Slovenia's AFIR target attainment figures were not found on a reachable page.
The official PDF of the JRPM IZVEN-TEN-T-2026 call on gov.si returned a 503 error; its details come from an installer's summary.
No official source was found confirming whether any household electricity price regulation applies in 2026 (the last decree ended on 28.2.2025).
Borzen JP SUB-EV26 still shows as open with an over-subscription notice; media report the money ran out in August 2026, but no formal closure notice was found.

No 2026 legal change giving apartment residents a 'right to plug' (for example, transposition of the recast EU buildings directive) was confirmed; the only charging reference found in the SZ-1G amendment is the shared charging station listed as a common part.
The Efficient Use of Energy Act (ZURE) rules on chargers and ducting in buildings were not checked on an official source (the legal database returned an error); the summary comes from Avto magazin.
GEN-I's e-mobility page shows no home-charger offer; home-charger offers of E 3 and Elektro energija were not found.

The installer site e-mobilni.eu timed out and elektricna-polnilnica.si did not resolve; online-only shops such as evmotions.si (operated by a Hungarian company) and marketplaces were not included as companies.
